reason: In lucide-react 1.57.0 FlipHorizontal2 and FlipVertical2 are plain alias exports of TrianglesCenterlineDashedHorizontal/Vertical with no @deprecated tag (TypeScript 6 reports no 6385/6387 suggestion) and rendering them emits no warning, so a test cannot tell the old names from the new.

The only difference (checked in jsdom against 19.1.0) is that a focused <input type=number> now gets its value attribute/defaultValue updated on re-render instead of after blur, which the displayed value and form reset only reveal in a focused-then-reset-without-re-render corner; tried uncontrolled defaultValue updates, controlled value syncing and form.reset(), and code written for 19.1 is the same JSX as for 19.3, so no plausible application code depends on the old behavior.

Confirmed in jsdom (a suspending tab switch and a search-box update in separate startTransition calls: 19.1.0 holds the search update until the tab resolves, 19.3.1 commits it at once), but the new behavior only removes a delay, so code written for 19.1 (both updates in transitions, or the input as a sync update) works unchanged on 19.3 and the only code that would break expects two separate transitions to commit together, which no plausible application relies on.

In lucide-react 1.57.0 Angry, Annoyed, Laugh, Meh, Frown and Smile are plain alias exports of the new Face* icons with no @deprecated tag (TypeScript 6 reports no 6385/6387 suggestion) and rendering them emits no warning, so a test cannot tell the old names from the new.

lucide-react 1.57.0 no longer exports RailSymbol at all (TypeScript: no exported member RailSymbol), because it was removed with the brand icons at 1.0.1, which is the separate population entry lucide-react@1.0.1/brand-icons-removed, so the pinned version has no deprecated RailSymbol whose deprecation a task could test.

The change is only a DEV console.error (warnForReactChildrenConflict in react-dom-client.development.js, absent from the production build and from 19.1.0) when a React-owned element that sets text children or dangerouslySetInnerHTML is used as a createRoot/createPortal container; rendering behaves the same, so it is logging that application code cannot depend on.
